messages:
alex: FYI cost-alert — us-west1 GPU spend spiked ~3.5x in the last 45m. Noticed a lot of new GPU nodes coming up, digging in. :grimacing:
costops-bot: Automated alert: project/redwood-prod - gpu_compute charges increased by $62k in 1h. See https://billing.cloud/summary/xyz and run `gcloud compute instances list --filter="zone:(us-west1)"`.
marie: I pulled the infra events. Hundreds of nodes launched in pool 'gpu-heavy-io'. Many are `a2-highmem-8`.
sanjay: Provisioner logs show NodeTemplate selection preferred `a2-*` family because of a label mismatch: our terraform applied `labels = { gpu_family = "a2" }` to the pool after a merge yesterday. Should be `a100` family that maps to our commitments.
alex: Oof — commitments/Reservations are for a100-family. These a2s are on-demand => no committed discount. That's why cost jumped so hard.
marie: Quick mitigation: scaling the pool down and cordoning the new nodes. Commands: `kubectl get nodes -l role=gpu-heavy-io -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Doing in batches.
sanjay: Pushing a hotfix to infra: changed `nodeSelector` and `labels.gpu_family` back to `a100`. Also added a guard in the provisioner to prefer instance families that match `commitment_sku`. Patch:```hcl
resource "google_compute_instance_template" "gpu" {
  labels = {
    gpu_family = "a100" # was a2 due to bad merge
  }
  # ...
}
```
marie: Also added an admission check to reject pods that request >512GB mem with no `gpu_type` annotation. We saw some custom jobs requesting huge memory which leaned the scheduler toward memory-optimized a2s.
tess: Have we opened a billing support case to recover credits for the window where reserved commitment could have applied if the right SKUs were used?
costops-bot: Billing case created: CASE-122349. Cloud support acknowledged and requested detailed instance/usage mapping for the period 2026-03-17 02:00-03:00 UTC. They may consider prorated adjustments.
jaime: I can run the query to map instance IDs -> SKU -> commit family and attach to the case. Running: `gcloud billing accounts projects sku-usage list --start-time=2026-03-17T02:00:00Z --end-time=2026-03-17T03:00:00Z --format=json > /tmp/sku-usage.json`
sanjay: Heads up — we should also add a cost-guard in the autoscaler: a hard cap on concurrent launches per minute and a whitelist of allowed instance families per region. I'll open a PR.
alex: I've rolled the autoscaler config back to the previous commit for now and set maxSurgeLaunches: 8. Monitoring CPU/gpu utilization + cloud spend.
marie: After cordons/drains and rollback we stopped new a2 launches. Spend trend is dropping, but still waiting on the billing case.
tess: Action items: 1) jaime -> attach SKU mapping to CASE-122349, 2) sanjay -> PR to add family whitelist + rate limit, 3) marie -> admission webhook merged, 4) alex -> monitor for 4h and escalate if any new spikes.
marie: Filing an infra postmortem draft in #postmortems with timeline and root cause (merge changed label -> provisioner picked a2 -> on-demand billing).
alex: Good catch everyone. Add a retrospective note to stop-merge checklist: verify `labels.gpu_family` matches `commitment_sku` for any change touching node templates. :memo:
